title: Harden inbound email parsing: ambiguous From forms, attribute text, bidi filenames
description: Non-blocking findings from the focused re-review of the inbound email parsing PR, to fix before the ingress Lambda is wired (M1.8) or in M2 at the latest. (1) Sender ambiguity: a From with an unquoted address followed by an angle-bracket address, a display name that contains an at sign, or two address-like tokens is accepted as the angle-bracket address; the receiver DMARC verdict could refer to the other one. Refuse when the display name contains an at sign or more than one address-like token appears in the raw From; also refuse obsolete route syntax and multi-at forms outright instead of relying on identity lookup. (2) html-to-text ends a tag at the first closing angle bracket, so a closing angle bracket inside a quoted attribute leaks the rest of the attribute as body text; make the tag scanner quote-aware. (3) sanitizedAttachmentFileName does not strip bidirectional override characters such as U+202E. (4) When a reply is dropped as sender_not_in_conversation the sender's own conversation-key index entry has already been written; write it only after admission. Gherkin first, red then green. Origin: review of PR 644.
